what: scripts/load_router.py, real q15_r16 student on vLLM (RTX 3060 Laptop, on AC power), TEACHER_ENABLED=false, rate limit off, 1 router process. 503s are the student's invalid outputs with the teacher off (~4%, matching the 4.3% invalid rate on test), not errors.

host_path.path: Windows host -> Docker Desktop/WSL2 port forward (127.0.0.1:8115) -> router container -> vLLM container
host_path.note: c=128 collapsed: 7.2 ok/s, p95 5.4 s, 398 of 1500 requests failed at the transport level. Docker Desktop's engine became unresponsive right after (docker _ping -> HTTP 500), so the c=256 row (all transport errors) is not a measurement of the router.

in_network.path: load generator container on the compose network -> router container -> vLLM container (no Windows/WSL2 port forward)

runs.config: guarded MAX_INFLIGHT=16 MAX_QUEUE=16 (repeat, docker stats sampled mid-run: router 20.8% CPU, vLLM 124.8% CPU, load generator 67.4% CPU; GPU 80% util, 61 W, 1507 MHz)

findings: Same c=128 load with no port forward: 0 transport errors and 68 ok/s (vs 398 errors and 7.2 ok/s through the port forward). The c>64 collapse is in the host-side path, as the README suspected; the GPU path degrades (p95 ~5 s) but does not fail.

Admission control works as designed (8.5-14% of requests got a 429 with Retry-After: 1, no transport errors), but on this box it did NOT lower the p95 of admitted requests (5.1 s unguarded vs 5.3-5.5 s guarded) and throughput was 6-15% lower. Negative result: the extra latency is not explained by router or vLLM queueing (16 in flight should give well under 1 s); the client-side load generator (67% CPU) and Docker Desktop networking are suspects; not isolated.
Admission control cannot protect a proxy in front of the router (the WSL2 port forward); on Cloud Run that layer is Google's front end plus max_instance_request_concurrency.
